req.title: Update requires title
req.statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /<id>/update omits the title.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update must render 'Title is required.' when the title field is omitted. We need: (1) a positive case confirming a valid update with title succeeds (HTTP 2xx/302, no error), (2) a negative case confirming that omitting the title yields HTTP 200 with 'Title is required.' in the response body, (3) a boundary case confirming that an empty-string title (the exact boundary between present and absent) also triggers the error. We also add a case for a single-space title to test the boundary of falsy vs truthy strings, and a state-transition case to confirm the post is NOT updated in the DB when title is missing. All tests use the pre-loaded fixture data (user id=1, post id=1) and log in as 'test'/'test'.

tests.name: test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds
preconditions: App initialized with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database pre-loaded with user id=1 (test/test) and post id=1
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /1/update with title='Updated Title', body='Updated body'
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-018: positive path — title present, update succeeds
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds()

tests.name: test_update_missing_title_does_not_persist_change
preconditions: App initialized with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database pre-loaded with user id=1 (test/test) and post id=1 with title='test title'
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /1/update with title='', body='new body' (empty title)
GET /1/update to verify the post title is unchanged in the DB
expected: POST /1/update returns HTTP 200 with 'Title is required.'
Subsequent GET /1/update still shows original title 'test title' in the page
The database row is NOT mutated
trace: R-FLASKR-018: state-transition — failed validation must not commit DB changes; catches mutations that remove the `if error is not None` guard

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_missing_title_does_not_persist_change():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': '', 'body': 'new body'})
